features.entity_name: SURF 4850 Level — LBNF/DUNE far detector caverns
features.method: Derived. Inputs: (1) the four published 4850L LBNF Campus module coordinates of Heise (arXiv:2603.06504) Table 4, WGS 84 decimal degrees (the table prints its "Latitude" and "Longitude" column headings interchanged: the cells under "Latitude" carry the W longitudes, the hemisphere letters resolve it): FD1 (NE) -103.7546341, 44.3459914; FD2 (SE) -103.7548042, 44.3450261; FD3 (NW) -103.7556732, 44.3460857; FD4 (SW) -103.7558433, 44.3451204 (lon, lat). They form a rectangle 83.29 m by 108.19 m. (2) The TDR (Vol. III, section 5.2) puts the first detector in the east side of the north cavern and the second in the east side of the south cavern, so FD1 and FD3 share the north cavern and FD2 and FD4 the south cavern, and (Vol. IV, section 1) "one either side of the central access drift". The cavern centre is taken as the midpoint of FD1 and FD3; its long axis runs along the line joining them (initial bearing 277.23 deg, 277.23 deg for the other cavern). (3) The footprint is 521.5 ft x 65 ft = 158.95 m x 19.81 m, the as-excavated figure on a Fermilab LBNF/DUNE project slide of 12 Dec 2023, not the TDR design length of 144.5 m (see notes). No survey outline of the cavern exists in the sources found; edges and ends are idealised.
features.name: LBNF/DUNE north detector cavern, 4850 Level (FD1 east, FD3 west)

provenance.locator: Heise (arXiv:2603.06504) Table 4, 4850L LBNF Campus rows FD1 (NE), FD2 (SE), FD3 (NW), FD4 (SW)
provenance.note: Position: midpoint of two published module coordinates (a design-model table, not a cavern survey); the module points may be cryostat centres or pit centres, and the table does not say. Length: 158.95 m (Fermilab slide, 521.5 ft) agrees with the laser-scan area in Heise Table 2; the TDR design length is 144.5 m and cannot hold two 65.8 m cryostats whose published centres are 83.3 m apart.
